risks.title: Cyberattacks compromising sensitive data
risks.score_rationale: The risk ranks at the top of risk factors and is described as existential. The language is strong (risks associated with cyber threats). Dedicated governance (SPPO, audit committee) and quarterly board updates indicate high severity. Cybersecurity category is heavily weighted.

risks.title: Non-compliance with data protection regulations
risks.score_rationale: The risk is closely tied to cybersecurity and personal data. Repeated mention of GDPR, HIPAA, and other compliance requirements. The role of the DPO (30 years of experience) underscores its importance. Language emphasizes compliance obligations and risks of penalties.

risks.title: Dependence on key personnel expertise in cybersecurity
risks.score_rationale: Explicit mention of the Head of IT's experience (30 years) and the DPO's tenure (13 years at Certara). Their central roles in cyber governance and compliance indicate critical dependency. High risk but mitigated by the SPPO structure.

risks.title: Operational risks related to IT infrastructure
risks.score_rationale: SaaS technology company managing sensitive data. The text notes critical SaaS environments operating for 16 years. Any technical failure or system outage could disrupt services and damage trust.

risks.title: Undisclosed legal and contingent risks
risks.score_rationale: Reference to Note 11 on litigation, but no detailed information provided. Minimal mention in the 10-K, suggesting the risk is present but not acute. Category moderately weighted.

risks.title: Volatility of bookings in the biopharma industry
risks.score_rationale: The text emphasizes that bookings vary significantly based on the health of the biopharma sector. Explicitly states that bookings are not a reliable predictor of revenue. A recurring and central risk for financial predictability.

risks.title: Regulatory dependence and acceptance by authorities
risks.score_rationale: Acceptance by regulatory agencies (FDA, EMA) is critical for product and service demand. A reversal in acceptance trends could eliminate or substantially reduce demand for biosimulation services.

ai_positioning.summary: Certara explicitly integrates AI and machine learning into its biosimulation solutions. The approach centers on an 'expert-in-the-loop' model that deploys AI capabilities within validated scientific frameworks and expert-led workflows, rather than as autonomous automated systems. AI is used to automate biosimulation processes, create generative AI applications for regulatory documents, and enhance productivity and insight generation while maintaining scientific validity and transparency.
evidence: Our technology and scientists incorporate modern advances in scientific understanding, drug research and development experience, data analysis, and AI

Our approach to AI is grounded in our long-standing expertise in mechanistic and empirical modeling. We deploy AI capabilities within validated scientific frameworks and expert-led workflows, rather than as standalone automated systems.
This expert-in-the-loop model allows us to leverage native AI capabilities in a manner that is consistent with regulatory expectations for transparency, reproducibility, and explainability.
Native AI and machine learning technologies are being incorporated across our technology and consulting services portfolios

We are using machine learning to automate and speed the process of biosimulation, and we have created generative AI applications to aid in drafting regulatory documents from scientific analyses and clinical data.
We apply AI capabilities within established modeling environments and under the supervision of experienced scientists and regulatory experts.
